stem: Which transmission mode allows data to travel in both directions, but only in one direction at a time?

options.rationale: Correct: both ways, taking turns.
Simplex allows one direction only.
Full-duplex allows both directions at the same time.
Parallel describes how many bits travel at once, not the direction.

explanation: Simplex: one way. Half-duplex: both ways, one at a time. Full-duplex: both ways at once.

options.content: Bits are sent one at a time along a single wire
options.rationale: Correct.

options.content: Several bits are sent at once on separate wires
options.rationale: That is parallel transmission.

options.content: Data is sent in one direction only
options.rationale: That is simplex, a transmission mode.

options.content: Data is sent in both directions at once
options.rationale: That is full-duplex.

explanation: Serial: one bit after another on one wire. Parallel: several bits simultaneously on several wires.

stem: Which is the best example of **full-duplex** transmission?

options.content: A television broadcast to many homes
options.rationale: Viewers cannot send data back: simplex.

options.content: A telephone call between two people
options.rationale: Correct: both people can speak and hear at the same time.
Users take turns to speak: half-duplex.

options.content: A sensor sending readings to a data logger
options.rationale: Readings travel one way only: simplex.

explanation: Full-duplex means both directions at the same time, as in a phone call.

stem: Which is the best example of **simplex** transmission?

options.content: A video call between two branches
options.rationale: Both sides send and receive at once: full-duplex.

options.content: Two pilots taking turns on a radio channel
options.rationale: Both directions, one at a time: half-duplex.

options.content: Browsing the web on a phone
options.rationale: Requests go up and pages come down, so not simplex.

options.content: A radio station broadcasting to listeners
options.rationale: Correct: data travels from the station to the radios only.

explanation: Simplex is one direction only, such as a broadcast.

stem: Why is parallel transmission unsuitable over long distances?

options.content: Parallel transmission can only send data one way
options.rationale: Parallel describes the number of wires, not the direction.

options.content: Parallel cables carry only one bit at a time
options.rationale: Parallel carries several bits at once.

options.content: The bits can arrive at slightly different times (skew)
options.rationale: Correct: over long wires, bits sent together get out of step.

options.content: Parallel signals cannot be sent through copper wire
options.rationale: Parallel links do use copper wires.

explanation: Over long cables, small differences between wires cause skew; neighbouring wires can also interfere (crosstalk). Parallel also needs more expensive cable.

stem: Inside a computer, data moves between the processor and memory over a distance of a few centimetres, and speed matters most. Which method is most suitable?

options.rationale: Serial sends one bit at a time; over a few centimetres parallel is faster.
Data must travel both to and from memory, and simplex is a direction, not the number of wires.
An echo check is an error-detection method, not a transmission method.
Correct: over a very short distance, sending several bits at once is fast and skew is not a problem.

explanation: Parallel transmission is suited to very short distances where its speed is an advantage and skew does not arise; this is why internal buses are parallel.
hints: Think about distance and the number of bits sent at once.

stem: Rudo says: "Serial transmission is always slower than parallel transmission." Which response is best?

options.content: Yes: serial can never be faster because it sends one bit at a time
options.rationale: Modern serial links are very fast; over distance they beat parallel.

options.content: No: serial sends several bits at once, so it is always faster
options.rationale: Serial sends one bit at a time.

options.content: Yes: serial transmission works in one direction only
options.rationale: Serial can be simplex, half- or full-duplex.

options.content: Not always: over long distances fast serial links are more reliable and can be faster
options.rationale: Correct: parallel loses its advantage over distance because of skew and crosstalk.

explanation: Over short distances parallel is faster, but over long distances skew and interference limit it, so high-speed serial is used (for example USB and network links).
hints: What limits parallel transmission over long cables?

stem: In half-duplex transmission, data can never be sent back to the device that sent the first message.
explanation: False. Half-duplex allows data in both directions; the directions just take turns. One-direction-only is simplex.

stem: A serial cable is usually cheaper than a parallel cable of the same length.
explanation: True. Serial needs fewer wires and smaller connectors, so the cable costs less.

stem: Match each situation to its transmission mode.

left.content: A sensor sends temperatures to a data logger; nothing is sent back
Two field rangers at Hwange talk on radios and say "over" when they finish
A broadband connection downloads a video while uploading photos

explanation: One way only: simplex. Both ways, taking turns: half-duplex. Both ways at once: full-duplex.

stem: Match each statement to serial or parallel transmission.

left.content: Sends one bit at a time on one wire
Sends several bits at once on several wires
Bits can become skewed over long cables
Used by USB connections and long network links
Used by internal buses inside the computer

explanation: Serial: one bit at a time, used over long distances (USB, network links). Parallel: several bits at once, fast over very short distances (internal buses) but skewed over long cables.

stem: A device sends 5 bytes of data using **serial** transmission. How many bits must travel along the single data wire, one after another?
explanation: Each byte is 8 bits: $5 \times 8 = 40$ bits, sent one at a time.

stem: A parallel link has 8 data wires and sends one bit on each wire at a time. How many separate sends (one bit per wire each time) are needed to transfer 6 bytes?
explanation: 6 bytes = 48 bits; 48 ÷ 8 wires = 6 sends (one byte each time).
workedSolution:
1. Total bits: $6 \times 8 = 48$.
2. Bits per send: 8.
3. Sends: $48 \div 8 = 6$.
hints: Each send carries 8 bits, one on each wire.

payload.template: Over long distances, {{blank:a}} transmission is used because the bits in {{blank:b}} transmission can arrive out of step. A phone call is an example of {{blank:c}} transmission.

explanation: Serial for long distances (no skew); a phone call is full-duplex.

stem: A shop in Mutare connects a till to a computer in the back office using a 25 m cable. Explain why serial transmission is more suitable than parallel. [3]

points.description: The distance is long, and parallel bits would skew / arrive out of step
Serial has less interference (crosstalk) because there are fewer wires

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Over 25 m the bits of a parallel transmission would arrive at slightly different times (skew), corrupting the data. Serial uses fewer wires, so there is less crosstalk, and the cable is cheaper.

explanation: Distance, interference and cost all favour serial.

stem: A car-park barrier at a shopping centre in Harare sends "car waiting" signals to a control computer, which sends back "open" commands. The two never need to be sent at the same moment. Suggest a suitable transmission mode and justify your choice. [2]

points.description: Data must travel both ways, but not at the same time (so the simpler half-duplex is sufficient)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Half-duplex, because signals must go both ways (requests and commands) but never at the same time.

explanation: Both directions, taking turns: half-duplex. Full-duplex would also work but is not needed.
hints: Does the data need to go both ways? At the same time?

stem: A secondary school in Gweru has a weather station on its roof. Sensors send readings along a 60 m cable to a computer in the geography room. The computer never sends data back to the sensors. Students also use the computer for video lessons with a school in Bulawayo.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Which mode describes the link from the sensors to the computer?

options.rationale: Nothing is sent back to the sensors.
Correct: one direction only.
Nothing is sent back at all.
Parallel is not a direction mode.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Which mode is needed for the video lessons?

options.rationale: The schools must talk to each other.
Taking turns would make a live conversation awkward.
Correct: both schools send and receive at once.
Serial is not a direction mode.

parts.explanation: Both directions at the same time.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Explain why serial rather than parallel transmission should be used on the 60 m cable.

points.description: Over a long distance parallel bits suffer skew / arrive out of step
Serial uses fewer wires: less interference and cheaper cable

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Parallel bits would arrive out of step over 60 m, and serial cable has fewer wires, so it is cheaper and suffers less crosstalk.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Give **one** advantage and **one** disadvantage of parallel transmission.

points.description: Advantage: faster over short distances (several bits at once)
Disadvantage: skew / crosstalk over long distances, or more expensive cabling

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: It is faster over short distances because several bits travel at once, but over long cables the bits get out of step and the cable is expensive.

explanation: Sensors to computer: serial simplex. Video lesson: full-duplex.
hints: For each method, link your reason to distance or direction.

stem: A mining company near Zvishavane uses radio handsets underground. At the moment each handset can either transmit or receive, and the user presses a button to talk.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Which transmission mode do the handsets use now?

options.rationale: Users can reply, so it is not one-way.
Correct: both ways, one at a time.
Users cannot talk and listen at the same time.
Serial is not a mode of direction.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Describe the difference between half-duplex and full-duplex transmission.

points.description: Half-duplex: data both directions but only one direction at a time

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Half-duplex sends data both ways, but only one way at a time; full-duplex sends both ways at the same time.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Explain **one** benefit to the miners of changing to full-duplex handsets.

points.description: Both people can speak and listen at the same time
so an urgent warning can interrupt immediately / no waiting for the channel, which matters for safety

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Both people can talk at once, so a warning can be given immediately without waiting for the other person to finish, which is safer underground.

explanation: Press-to-talk radios are half-duplex; full-duplex allows simultaneous two-way speech.
hints: Define each mode before choosing one.
